model_names: 331 model with general beta (SU(3)C x SU(3)L x U(1)X; scalar triplets rho, eta, chi; heavy quarks D,S,T; heavy leptons E_l; gauge bosons Z', V, Y); studied at beta = +-sqrt(3), +-1/sqrt(3)
rows.reference_implements: 331.fr implements the general-beta 331 model of Sec. 2 with beta as an external parameter (Bet); this one file covers all four paper benchmarks. The sibling files 331_-1.fr, 331_1.fr, 331_-3.fr, 331_3.fr are the same model with beta hard-coded to -1/sqrt(3), +1/sqrt(3), -sqrt(3), +sqrt(3) and numeric charges.
evidence: Abstract: 'Four benchmark 331 models, beta = +-sqrt(3) and beta = +-1/sqrt(3), are studied in this work.' Sec. 1: 'different versions of the 331 model ... characterized by a parameter called beta.'

Sec. 2.1 Eq. (2.2)-(2.3): three Higgs triplets rho, eta, chi with vevs v1, v2, v3; Eq. (2.9) Higgs potential with lambda_i, lambda_ij, lambda'_ij and sqrt(2) f eps rho eta chi. Sec. 2.3 Eq. (2.56),(2.58): q1L,q2L triplets, q3L anti-triplet, all leptons anti-triplets with (e, -nu, E). Sec. 2.4 Eq. (2.61)-(2.62): Yukawa terms.
Sec. 2.5 Eq. (2.65)-(2.66) and Table 1: beta = +-n/sqrt(3), n=1,3 gives the four charge assignments; the field content is the same for every beta, only Q and X charges change.

Reference 331.fr header: 'FeynRules mod-file for the 331 model where beta is general'; M$vevs = {Rho[2],v},{Phi[1],v2},{Chi[3],v3}; beta == {ParameterType -> Internal, Value -> Bet}; charges written as Q -> 1/6-Sqrt[3] beta/2 (Jq12), Q -> 1/6+Sqrt[3] beta/2 (Jt), Q -> -1/2+Sqrt[3] beta/2 (EE). LHiggs and LYukawa match Eq. (2.9) and Eq. (2.61)-(2.62).
rows.notes: The paper defines one model: the 331 gauge extension with one fixed field content (three scalar triplets, two quark triplets plus one anti-triplet, three lepton anti-triplets, right-handed singlets for u, d, D/S/T, e, E) and one Lagrangian (Eqs. 2.8-2.9, 2.32, 2.54, 2.60-2.62). The parameter beta only sets the U(1)X and electric charges of the new states. This is the 'one-parameter family of U(1) charges' case in the definition, so it is single-model. The four benchmarks beta = +-sqrt(3), +-1/sqrt(3) are parameter points, not separate models. The scored reference 331.fr keeps beta general (external parameter Bet), so it matches the paper's Sec. 2 directly and covers all four benchmarks. It adds no fields beyond the paper; ghosts and Goldstones are gauge-fixing content (Feynman gauge), not new physics. Confusion risk is medium, not low, for two reasons. First, the abstract and text call the four beta choices 'benchmark 331 models' and 'different versions', so an agent may hard-code one beta value with integer charges (as the sibling files do) instead of the general-beta form the reference uses; field names and Q/X values would then differ from 331.fr. Second, the paper lists Feynman rules in unitary gauge (Appendix A) while the reference uses Feynman gauge with ghosts. Neither choice changes the field content or symmetry, so the model itself is the same. Naming differences: the reference calls the eta triplet Phi and the rho vev v (paper: v1).

model_names: Sextet fermion qg-portal model (eq. 12: Psi_u, Psi_d)
Sextet scalar q-lepton-g model (eq. 13: Phi_u, Phi_d)
rows.reference_implements: all-in-one
evidence: Intro (Sec. I): 'we construct two simplified models of color-sextet fields and explore the phenomenology of these particles at the LHC'; abstract instead says 'a simple but novel model of color-sextet fields'.

Sec. III eq. (12): 'The sextet fermion models are defined by L ⊃ Ψ̄_q(iD̸−m)Ψ_q + (1/Λ)[κ J^{sia}(q^c_R σ^{μν} Ψ_q) G + H.c.] + (1/Λ³)[κ_B J(q^c_R Ψ_q) B G + H.c.]' for q ∈ {u,d}; eq. (13) scalars: '(1/Λ²)[λ J Φ_q (q^c_R σ^{μν} ℓ_R) G + H.c.]'.

Table X ('Exotic field content of color-sextet models considered in Section III'): Φu (6,1,1/3) L=−1; Φd (6,1,4/3) L=−1; Ψu (6,1,−2/3) L=0; Ψd (6,1,1/3) L=0. Then: 'We implement these simplified models in version 2.3.43 of FeynRules'.

Reference header: 'sFu = (6, 1, -2/3); sFd = (6, 1, 1/3); sSu = (6, 1, 1/3) (Lepton number -1); sSd = (6, 1, 4/3) (Lepton number -1)'; Lagrangian 'LSextet := LSextetKin + LFu + LFd + LSu + LSd' with CFu/CFBu/CFd/CFBd/CSu/CSd couplings matching eqs. (12)-(13).
refuter_reasons: The classifier counts the sextet-fermion sector (eq. 12) and the sextet-scalar sector (eq. 13) as two models. Under the working definition a paper is multi-model only when it offers distinct alternatives an implementer must choose between. This paper offers no such choice. Section III fixes ONE field content (Table X: Phi_u, Phi_d, Psi_u, Psi_d, all present together), ONE symmetry structure (SM gauge group plus accidental lepton number), and one Lagrangian (the sum of eqs. 12 and 13 for q=u,d). The paper states it implements 'these simplified models' in a single FeynRules implementation, and the reference file by co-author Murphy is exactly that union: four fields with the Table X charges and LSextet := LSextetKin + LFu + LFd + LSu + LSd, with no extra operators or fields. The fermion and scalar sectors do not couple to each other in eqs. (12)-(13), so they are decoupled sub-sectors of one Lagrangian, not competing alternatives; studying them separately (Figs. 3-4 vs Fig. 5) is analogous to studying special cases of one model. The paper's own wording is inconsistent and cannot be used to count: the abstract says 'a simple but novel model', the intro says 'two simplified models' and, two paragraphs later, 'a simplified model of color-sextet scalars and fermions' (singular, containing both species). Taking the plural literally would also give 4 models, since eq. (12) says 'the sextet fermion models ... for q in {u,d}', so the classifier's choice of 2 is a partial literal reading. The classifier itself concedes that the field content is unambiguous and that the page can be reclassified as single-model; with an all-in-one reference that is not a superset and no implementer choice, the correct verdict is single-model, n_models=1. Section II is an operator catalog with generic hypercharges, not a set of defined models, and Section III explicitly picks 'a small subset' of it; it does not change the count.

The classifier counts two models because the intro says "two simplified models". The benchmark definition does not count by the paper's words. It counts by alternatives an implementer must choose between. This paper gives no such choice. Table X fixes one particle content: Phi_u (6,1,1/3), Phi_d (6,1,4/3), Psi_u (6,1,-2/3), Psi_d (6,1,1/3). Eqs. (12) and (13) give one Lagrangian for these four fields under one symmetry structure (SM gauge group plus lepton number). The scalar and fermion sextets are not alternatives for the same state. They have different hypercharges and lepton numbers, and the paper simulates all four together (Fig. 2 pair production of both spins, Figs. 3-4 fermions, Fig. 5 scalars). The reference implementation confirms this. It is one file with one M$ModelName ("368_sextets"), one Lagrangian LSextet = LSextetKin + LFu + LFd + LSu + LSd, and exactly the four Table X fields. The FeynRules author (paper co-author T. Murphy) lists all four as "The new particles" and does not describe variants or a choice. The reference contains exactly the eq. (12)-(13) operators: no |H|^2 G term, no diquark operators, no extra fields. It is not a superset and not a subset. The paper's own model-count language is inconsistent (abstract: "a simple but novel model"; intro: "two simplified models" and "a simplified model of color-sextet scalars and fermions"; Sec. III: "the sextet fermion models" for q in {u,d}), so it cannot fix the count. The Psi_u focus in Fig. 6 is a special case of the one model, which the definition says stays single-model. Verdict: single model, n_models = 1.
rows.notes: The paper has two layers. Section II is a catalog of EFT operators for color sextets (not a model: generic hypercharges, ~100 operators). Section III picks the 3⊗6⊗8 invariant and defines two simplified models: a sextet fermion model (eq. 12, with up- and down-type copies Ψu, Ψd) and a sextet scalar model (eq. 13, with Φu, Φd). The paper calls them 'two simplified models' but presents all four fields together in Table X and implements them together in FeynRules. The sectors do not couple to each other, so the union is one consistent Lagrangian. The benchmark reference (by co-author T. Murphy) is exactly this union: four fields with the Table X charges and lepton numbers, kinetic terms, and the eq. (12)/(13) operators built with J^{sia} = -i√2 L t3 K̄ per eq. (A18) (K6, T, K3bar). No |H|^2 operator, no diquark (3⊗3⊗6bar) operators, no extra fields: not a superset. Cutoffs Λ are absorbed into the couplings (CFu etc.); Λ is not a separate parameter. Confusion risk is medium: (a) an agent could implement only the fermion sector or only Ψu, since the abstract says 'a model' and the phenomenology and Fig. 6 focus on Ψu, while the scalars are 'neglected so far'; (b) an agent could over-implement operators from Tables VIII/IX (e.g. the |H|^2 G term or diquark couplings); (c) the J^{sia} tensor must be built from FeynRules' K6/K3 objects, which is an implementation trap rather than a model-choice trap. The most natural reading of Table X plus 'We implement these simplified models' leads to the reference's four-field content, so most agents should converge on it. If the orchestrator prefers to treat a decoupled union that the authors implemented as one file as a single model, this page can be reclassified as single-model with n_models=1; the field content is unambiguous either way.

model_names: ALRSM (alternative left-right symmetric model: SU(3)c x SU(2)L x SU(2)R' x U(1)B-L gauge group plus global U(1)S)
rows.reference_implements: ALRSM
evidence: Abstract: 'We perform a consistent analysis of the alternative left-right symmetric model emerging from E6 grand unification.'

Sec. 2: 'It is based on the SU(3)c x SU(2)L x SU(2)R' x U(1)B-L gauge group, to which we supplement a global U(1)S symmetry'; Table 1 lists the full field content (QL, QR, d'L, dR, LL, LR, nL, nuR; phi, chiL, chiR; G, WL, WR, B). Eq. (2.3) gives the Yukawa Lagrangian, eq. (2.4) the scalar potential, eq. (2.16) effective H0 couplings to gluons/photons.

Sec. 2: 'There are three different ways to embed SU(2)H into SU(3)H' (LRSM, ALRSM, Inert Doublet Model) ... 'We are interested here in the second option.' The LRSM and IDM are only mentioned as context, not offered as alternatives to implement.

Sec. 3: 'we have implemented the model presented in section 2 into FeynRules ... publicly released on the FeynRules model database' (footnote: ALRM_general). Sec. 6, Table 3: BM I, BM II, BM III are parameter points of the same model, not distinct models.
rows.notes: The paper defines exactly one model, the ALRSM, and the reference .fr is the authors' own FeynRules implementation of that model (same author, same field names, PDG codes, parameter names and Les Houches blocks as paper Tables 7-8; same Yukawa terms as eq. 2.3 and same potential as eq. 2.4, with lam1, mu1^2, mu2^2, lam4 derived per eqs. A.3 and A.10). The reference is not a superset: it contains nothing the paper does not define. Minor points that could cause small deviations but not a different model: (1) the reference file is a unitary-gauge variant ('uni' in the filename; no Goldstone bosons or electroweak ghosts are declared, only the gluon ghost), while the paper discusses Goldstones G0_1, G0_2, G+-_1, G+-_2 in eqs. 2.7-2.8 and stresses a correct Goldstone sector for Feynman-gauge tools, so an agent might add Goldstones; (2) the reference implements the generalised lepton number as a LNumber quantum number, which an agent might omit; (3) paper Table 7 has a typo for the H0_i PDG codes (25, 25, 45, 55) where the reference uses 25, 35, 45, 55; (4) the paper's three benchmark scenarios (Table 3) are parameter points only. The paper is unusually explicit (appendix C documents the FeynRules implementation), so an agent reading only the paper should reproduce the reference model.

model_names: Minimal gauged U(1)_B-L extension of the SM (Z' gauge boson, SM-singlet scalar chi with B-L charge +2, three RH Majorana neutrinos with B-L charge -1; kinetic mixing g-tilde = 0)
rows.reference_implements: The paper's single model: the minimal (pure) B-L model with no U(1)_Y-U(1)_B-L kinetic mixing. B-L.fr (Basso & Pruna, 'pure B-L model' v1.1) has gauge groups SU3C x SU2L x U1Y x U1BL with one coupling g1p, fields Zp (plus Bp/ghZp/ghBp/phip gauge artefacts), H2 (second Higgs mixed with H1 via Sa/Ca), and three heavy Majorana neutrinos nH mixed with light nL; x = MZp/(2 g1p), matching the paper's x = MZ'/(2 g'1).
evidence: Paper Sec. 2: 'In addition to the particle content of the SM, the U(1)B-L model contains an Abelian gauge field B'_mu, a SM singlet scalar field chi and three RH neutrinos N_i' with charges Y_B-L = +2 and -1; Eqs. (2.2), (2.3), (2.5), (2.6) give the potential, covariant derivative, RH-neutrino kinetic term and Dirac+Majorana Yukawas.
Paper Sec. 2: 'we omit the Abelian mixing between U(1)B-L and U(1)Y, g-tilde = 0, as a simplification. This means we consider the minimal gauged B-L model.'

Paper Sec. 3.4 / Table 1: 'six extra free parameters' (MZ', g'1, Mh2, sin alpha, MNi, VlN); Cases A-E are parameter choices and scans of the same model; Sec. 2 says the Z'-only, singlet-scalar-only and singlet-neutrino-only scenarios arise 'by taking an appropriate limit'.

Reference B-L.fr header: 'This is the FeynRules mod-file for the pure B-L model', Authors Basso & Pruna, ref. arXiv:0812.4313; M$GaugeGroups has U1BL {GaugeBoson -> Bp, Charge -> BL, CouplingConstant -> g1p} and no gt parameter; M$ClassesDescription has nH (Heavy neutrino 1-3, SelfConjugate), Zp (PDG 9900032), H2 (PDG 9900026), phip Goldstone of Zp.
rows.notes: The paper is a phenomenology/Contur study of one UV-complete model. Cases A-E in Table 1 are benchmark parameter slices, not separate models. The other reference files: B-L_4.fr and B-L-N_4.fr are Wei Liu's (paper co-author) 2019 rewrites of the same model, differing only in whether the neutrino mixing is external or internal; minimal_Zp.fr (Basso) is the general U(1)' model with a Z-Z' kinetic-mixing coupling gt, which the paper explicitly switches off (g-tilde = 0), so B-L.fr is the correct benchmark. Field content of B-L.fr matches the paper exactly; the Feynman-gauge Goldstones and ghosts are gauge-fixing artefacts, and the CKM matrix is SM. Minor sources of implementation (not model) divergence for an agent: (1) Eq. (2.3) and the Appendix 7.1 RGEs keep the g-tilde term, so an agent might add a kinetic-mixing parameter fixed to zero; (2) the reference diagonalises the per-generation 2x2 seesaw into nL/nH mass eigenstates with San/Can (Eq. 2.9 of the paper) and uses diagonal Yukawas, which the paper adopts as its simplification; an agent could instead write the general 3x3 Yukawas of Eq. (2.6) without diagonalisation. Neither changes the field content or symmetry structure.

Sec. 5 Conclusions: 'investigate models whose particle content depend on the point in parameter space, which is however a separate project and will be presented elsewhere [54]' — the HEIDI study was removed from this version.
grep for heidi|golden|extra dimension|bulk|compact in the paper text: zero hits (only 'Kaluza-Klein' once, describing the Three-Site model).
rows.notes: Version mismatch between the benchmark text and the reference. The text is arXiv:1010.3251v2, which was retitled and stripped of the HEIDI physics; it is a pure interface/tool paper. The reference HEIDI.fr (plus HEIDI_bundle.fr, which bundles the Hdecay` width table and the Heidi` numerical spectrum calculator) implements the HEIDI model from v1: the SM Higgs replaced by a tower of n scalar modes Hh[k] with numerically computed masses, widths and wavefunction xi[k], unitarity gauge only, plus an optional effective ggh coupling. Nothing in the v2 text lets an agent reconstruct this: no field content, no Lagrangian, no parameters (compactification scale, bulk mass, 5D coupling, cutoff). An agent reading only the paper would most likely produce the Three-Site Higgsless Model (the only BSM model whose spectrum is described: W', Z', heavy fermions, nonlinear sigma field Eq. (1)), or the MSSM, or a plain SM export. Any of these would score against a reference with a completely different field set. Recommend either swapping the text for arXiv:1010.3251v1 or dropping/relabelling this page.

model_names: SM + anomalous U(1)_X vector boson X with D'Hoker-Farhi/Chern-Simons couplings c1 (XZZ, XZgamma) and c2 (XWW)
rows.reference_implements: The low-energy effective model of Sec. 2 (eq. 1, eq. 5) and Sec. 5 (vertices eqs. 27-28): SM plus one neutral massive vector xb. The reference reparametrizes the couplings (cW, cZ, cZgamma instead of c1, c2) and adds a Cmu muon coupling the paper does not have. The file declares only the field and parameters; it contains no Lagrangian.
evidence: Abstract: 'If the new fermions have SM charges, but are too heavy to be created at LHC, and the SM fermions are not charged under the extra gauge field'
Sec. 2, eq. (1): 'At energies accessible at LHC and below the masses of the new heavy fermions, the theory in question is simply the SM plus a massive vector boson X' with Stueckelberg field theta_X
Sec. 2, eq. (5): L_int = c1 (H^dag DH/|H|^2) Dtheta_X F_Y + c2 (H F_W DH^dag/|H|^2) Dtheta_X; Sec. 5 eqs. (27)-(28): XZZ and XZgamma vertices are both proportional to c1, XW+W- to c2

Sec. 4, Tables 4-5, eq. (24): realistic SU(2)xU(1)_YxU(1)_X UV completion with heavy chiral fermions psi1, psi2, chi1, chi2 (doublets and singlets) and heavy Higgs Phi, 'all states have heavy masses ~ F<Phi>' above 10 TeV; presented as the origin of c1, c2, not as a separate model to simulate
rows.notes: The paper studies one model at collider energies: the SM plus one neutral massive vector X with dimension-4 anomaly-induced couplings to ZZ, Zgamma and WW. Two free couplings c1 and c2 control these vertices. The heavy fermion sectors are derivations, not alternatives: Sec. 2 gives a toy U(1)_A x U(1)_B model (Table 1), Sec. 3 a toy U(1)_Y x U(1)_X model with 4 Dirac fermions (Tables 2-3), and Sec. 4 a realistic SU(2) x U(1)_Y x U(1)_X charge assignment (Tables 4-5). All heavy states sit above 10 TeV and never enter the phenomenology of Sec. 5, so I count them as one model with a UV explanation. Reference file issues: (1) It has no Lagrangian at all, only M$ClassesDescription and M$Parameters, so any Lagrangian-level scoring against it is ill-defined. (2) It uses three independent couplings cW, cZ, cZgamma. The paper uses two: c1 fixes XZZ and XZgamma with a fixed ratio (sin theta_w / 2 vs cos theta_w), and c2 fixes XWW. (3) It adds Cmu, an X-muon coupling. The paper states SM fermions are neutral under U(1)_X, so this is a sector the paper never defines. This is why reference_is_superset is true, although the reference is a minimal file, not a large library. Confusion risk is medium: an agent that reads only the paper will get the field content right (one self-conjugate massive vector), but it will likely name and count the couplings as c1, c2 (not cW, cZ, cZgamma, Cmu), and it may try to implement the Stueckelberg field theta_X or the Sec. 4 heavy fermions and Phi as explicit fields.

Kraml et al., arXiv:1701.07008"}; fields Xr (real scalar DM), Xd (Dirac DM), Xv (vector DM), T[1] Y2 'Spin-2 mediator' coupled to the full SM energy-momentum tensor (gTg, gTw, gTb, gTq, gTq3, gTl, gTh) with cut-off Lambda.

rows.notes: Paper 1508.00564 (Mattelaer, Vryonidou) is multi-model: two distinct mediator alternatives (spin-0 Y0 vs spin-1 Y1) with Dirac DM, each with two coupling scenarios (S/P and V/A) that are parameter choices, not separate models. Eq. (3) also quotes the infinite-top-mass gluon EFT Lagrangian (gS_t alpha_s/(12 pi v) G G Y0 + gP_t alpha_s/(8 pi v) G Gtilde Y0) but only as a limit used for comparison in Fig. 9, so I do not count it as a third model. The benchmark reference dm_s_spin2.fr is a mismatch, not merely a superset: it implements the DMsimp spin-2 model of Das et al. 1605.09359 (Y2 tensor mediator coupled to T_mu_nu of every SM sector, plus real-scalar, Dirac, and vector DM) and contains neither Y0 nor Y1. An agent reading only this paper will write a scalar or vector mediator model and cannot reproduce the spin-2 reference. The paper's own models are in dm_s_spin0.fr and dm_s_spin1.fr (both cite 1508.00564); those files are themselves supersets (Xr/Xc scalar DM, couplings to all six quark flavours, gluon EFT operators gSg/gPg with Lambda, and in spin-1 also lepton, neutrino and flavour-changing monotop couplings; the _ew.fr files add h/W/B couplings). Recommendation: re-point this benchmark page to dm_s_spin0.fr or dm_s_spin1.fr, or split it into two pages, one per mediator spin.

model_names: Effective LRSM (SM + WR, ZR, three Majorana N)
rows.reference_implements: Effective LRSM (SM + WR, ZR, three Majorana N)
evidence: Sec. II: 'The Effective LRSM field content consists of the usual SM states, the W±R and ZR gauge bosons ... and three heavy Majorana neutrinos Ni, aligned with the RH chiral states.'

Sec. III A: 'We implement the SM Lagrangian ... in the Feynman gauge and the Lagrangian terms of Eqs. (4)-(8) in the Unitary gauge into FR 2.3.10' (Eq. 4: WR-q-q' with kappa_R^q and V_CKM'; Eq. 5: WR-l-N with Y_lN; Eq. 8-10: ZR neutral currents with g_L/g_R coefficients)

Reference header: 'Contains WR^+/- and ZR gauge bosons as well as three massive Majorana neutrinos ... SM Lagrangian is written in the Feynman Gauge. LRSM Extension is written in Unitary gauge'; References -> 'O. Mattelaer, et. al., [arXiv:1610.XXXXX]' (same authors as 1610.08985)

Reference M$ClassesDescription: V[32] ZR (MZR 5070), V[34] WR (MWR 3000, WWR 84.3), F[31] Nl = {N1,N2,N3} Majorana; LWRTmp and LZRTmp reproduce Eqs. (4), (5), (8)-(10) with kRq, kRl, VCKMR, YlN; matches Table II (MWR=3 TeV, Gamma_WR=84.3 GeV, MZR=5070, Gamma_ZR=114) and Eq. (19)
rows.notes: The paper is the release paper for this exact FeynRules model (EffLRSM@NLO, ref. [34]). It defines one model: SM + WR, ZR (mass eigenstates, no scalar sector, no non-Abelian VR self-couplings) + three Majorana N with WR charged currents (Eqs. 4-5) and ZR neutral currents (Eqs. 8-10). Parameter choices (kappa_R^q, kappa_R^l = 0.75 or 1; MWR scans; Eq. 19 masses) are benchmark points, not separate models. The reference file implements exactly these fields and terms; it is not a superset. Small places an agent could diverge from the reference, none of which change the model: (1) Eq. (5) contains a light-neutrino mixing term X_lm that Eq. (7) sets to zero and the reference omits, so an agent might add a WR-nu-l term with a zero parameter; (2) overall sign convention of the couplings (paper writes -kappa g/sqrt2, reference writes +ee/sw/Sqrt[2]); (3) the reference sets mN3 = 1e14 GeV while Eq. (19) uses 1e12 GeV for both N2 and N3 (benchmark value only); (4) an agent might be tempted to add VR self-interactions or the mass relation Eq. (18), which the paper explicitly excludes or treats as independent. The reference includes ZR couplings to light nu_L, consistent with Sec. II text and Table I.

rows.notes:
Classification. The paper presents three alternative spin hypotheses (scalar X0, vector X1, tensor X2) for one observed boson, each with its own Lagrangian L_J (eq. 2.1). The task definition lists 'spin-0 vs spin-1 vs spin-2' alternatives as multi-model, so n_models = 3. The 0+/0- and 1+/1- cases are parameter limits of the same field (alpha, eqs. 2.13-2.14), not separate models. The paper itself, however, calls the bundle one 'Higgs Characterisation model' and the reference implements all three fields in one file, so reference_implements = all-in-one.

Reference structure. HiggsCharacterisation.fr (v3.4, 17.10.2013, authors de Aquino and Mawatari) declares exactly the three paper fields X0 (PDG 5000000), X1 (5000001), X2 (5000002). It contains L0v (eq. 2.4 vector couplings, incl. the derivative kHda/kHdz/kHdw terms), L1 (eqs. 2.8, 2.11, 2.12 with kqa/kqb/kla/klb instead of the paper's kappa_fa/kappa_fb), and L2 (eqs. 2.15-2.16 with kq, kl, kg, ka, kz, kw). The Table 2 g couplings match (e.g. gHaa = 47 alpha/(18 pi v), gHgg = -alpha_s/(3 pi v)).

Superset caveats (minor, so flag set false). (a) L0v6: an effective gg X0 X0 vertex (kHHgg, kAAgg) added in v3.3 after the paper; the paper only says four-point operators are 'work in progress'. (b) Gauge-fixing terms TGFg/TGFa in the spin-2 E-M tensor, a MadGraph technicality the paper does not mention. (c) Full SM E-M tensors (W charged currents, MZ^2/MW^2 mass terms, Yukawa mass terms TYq/TYl) that the paper only cites from refs. [46, 48].

Why confusion risk is high. (1) The scored file omits eq. (2.2) (X0 Yukawa) and the kappa_SM ZZ/WW term; these are realised in the companion SM_HC.fr by renaming the SM Higgs to X0 (Phi[2] -> (vev + ca X0 + I G0)/Sqrt[2]) and inserting kSM, kHtt, kAtt etc. An agent reading only the paper will most likely write all of eqs. (2.2) and (2.4) into its new-physics file and keep or drop the SM Higgs H on its own judgement. (2) The paper gives only the QED E-M tensor; the spin-2 sector must be reconstructed from external references. (3) An agent may split the three spins into separate files or implement only one hypothesis. Field content (3 fields) is explicit in the paper, so the mismatch is mostly in Lagrangian placement and spin-2 details rather than in particle content.

Other reference files. HC.fr is v4.1 (2016) of the same all-in-one model with added kq3, X2-Z-A and X0 contact terms. HiggsCharacterization.fr is v2.0 (April 2013, pre-paper) with a different field list (X1, X1p, X0x, X2) and higher-dimension spin-2 operators the paper dropped. SM_HC.fr and SM_HC3.fr are the modified SM (Higgs renamed X0) that the HC files import as LSM.

Sec. 3: 'Having motivated the minimal set {G′, Z′, U1} of massive vectors ... We define the general Lagrangian for these vectors as follows' -> eqs. (9), (10), (11); coupling textures in eq. (13).

Sec. 3: 'We also ignore any possible interactions of the extra vectors among themselves and to any other particles related to the UV completion of the model (either scalars or fermions).' -> no vector-like fermions in the paper.
Sec. 4: 'we implement the model described in section 3 in FeynRules 2.3.32 ... available at https://feynrules.irmp.ucl.ac.be/wiki/LeptoQuark.'
rows.notes: The paper defines one model: the minimal vector set {U1 ~ (3,1,2/3), Z' ~ (1,1,0), G' ~ (8,1,0)} with a single phenomenological Lagrangian (eqs. 9-11), flavour textures (eq. 13), and free non-minimal gauge couplings kappa_U, kappa~_U, kappa_G', kappa~_G'. Section 2 discusses gauge vs strongly-interacting UV completions only as motivation; no second Lagrangian is written. Parameter benchmarks (beta_R^33 in {0, 0.5, 1}, kappa_U in {0,1}, widths) are scans, not separate models. The benchmark scores against VLferm.fr, which is the wrong file for this paper. VLferm.fr is a 2022 add-on by Fuentes-Martin and Faroughy (Faroughy is not a paper author). It adds SU(2) doublet vector-like fermions chiL ~ (1,2,-1/2) and chiQ ~ (3,2,1/6) with couplings to U1, Z', G' and mixing terms to 2nd/3rd generation SM fermions. It is not standalone: it uses VLQ, Zp, Gp, gU, gZp, gGp, and newCKM, which are declared in the other three files. An agent that reads only the paper will write vector_LQ + Zprime + coloron content and will never produce Ln/Le/Qu/Qd, so a mismatch is near certain. Recommendation: re-point the LeptoQuark reference to the set {vector_LQ.fr, Zprime.fr, coloron.fr} (or concatenate them), and drop VLferm.fr from the scored reference.

evidence: Abstract: 'It is then interpreted in the context of the next-to-minimal supersymmetric standard model and a dark supersymmetry model that allows for nonnegligible light boson lifetimes.'

Sec. 1: 'Two different classes of benchmark models are used ... the next-to-minimal supersymmetric standard model (NMSSM) [1, 5-12] and supersymmetry (SUSY) models with hidden sectors (dark SUSY) [3, 13, 14].' Also: 'This dark photon can couple to SM particles via a small kinetic mixing parameter epsilon with SM photons.'

Sec. 4: 'Higgs bosons are forced to decay to a pair of SUSY neutralinos n1 via h -> 2n1. Each SUSY neutralino in turn decays to a dark photon and a dark neutralino via n1 -> nD + gammaD. The dark neutralino mass mnD is set to 1 GeV' (mh=125, mn1=10 GeV; generated with MADGRAPH 4.5.2 + BRIDGE 2.24).
Sec. 1: 'A more thorough description of the NMSSM and dark SUSY models ... is included in Refs. [15] and [18].' The paper writes no Lagrangian and no field table for either model.
rows.notes: This is a CMS experimental search paper (model-independent limit), not a model-building paper. It uses two benchmark model classes with different field content: (1) NMSSM with h1/h2 and light pseudoscalar a1; (2) dark SUSY = MSSM plus a broken U(1)_D giving a dark photon gamma_D (kinetic mixing epsilon with the photon) and a dark neutralino nD. The paper defines neither model beyond decay topologies and mass points; it defers the model descriptions to Refs. [15] and [18]. The benchmark reference implements only the dark SUSY benchmark. The reference is a superset: it is the full FeynRules MSSM superfield implementation (squarks, sleptons, gluino, charginos, four neutralinos, 2HDM Higgs sector, soft terms, ghosts; 39 fields) plus the dark sector, whereas the paper's dark SUSY topology uses only h, n1, nD, gamma_D and muons. The reference also deviates from the paper's physics description: it has no kinetic-mixing parameter epsilon; instead it uses a direct vector coupling gd (=0.001) of AD to muons and a direct I*gd n1-nD-AD vertex, with the U(1)_D gaugino set to zero. An agent reading only the paper would have to choose between NMSSM and dark SUSY, would almost certainly write a simplified model (h, n1, nD, gamma_D, explicit h-n1-n1 coupling, epsilon F F_D kinetic mixing) rather than a full MSSM superfield file, and would not reproduce the reference's direct gd couplings. Confusion risk is therefore high.

rows.notes: The paper defines one model: the SM plus the d=5 Weinberg operator. It presents the same physics in two forms: (a) the gauge-invariant operator expanded after EWSB (Eqs. 5, 18-22) as Majorana bilinears of SM neutrinos, and (b) a practical prescription that models the LNV (nu_l nu^c_l') current as one unphysical Majorana neutrino N with universal couplings and mN = |sum C| v^2/Lambda (Eqs. 8, 9, 23-29). Form (b) is the implementation, not a separate model. The reference weinberg_NLO.fr implements form (b) exactly: one field N1, six real Wilson coefficients plus Lambda, internal mN1, and Lagrangian terms that match Eqs. (23)-(29) including the G+G+ l^c PL l' contact term (coefficient gw^2 mN/(4 MW^2) = 2 x gw^2 mN/(8 MW^2)). Surface convention differences: the reference writes the CC term with a + sign (paper Eq. 8/23 has -), and writes Goldstone terms in the Hermitian-conjugate form (lbar.ProjP.N1 GPbar, N1bar.ProjP.CC[l]) with +I. sm.fr is the stock SM 1.4.7 base that the paper says it extends; it is not extra content. The appendix and Table II are explicit enough that a careful agent should match the reference.

rows.notes: The paper (Zhang & Maltoni, t -> u_i h at NLO in QCD) defines one EFT: SM plus two dimension-six operators, O_uphi (flavour-changing Yukawa) and O_uG (flavour-changing chromomagnetic), each with four flavour structures (1,3),(3,1),(2,3),(3,2). No new fields, no new symmetry. The paper also writes two EOM-vanishing counterterm operators O(1), O(2) (Eqs. 33-34) but states they can be ignored; these are not a separate model. Special cases (focus on (1,3), Lambda = 1 TeV, real coefficients) are parameter choices, not separate models. The benchmark reference thu.fr implements exactly this operator set with the paper's normalisation (yt^3 for O_uphi, gs yt for O_uG, 1/Lambda^2) and is not a superset. The second file in the directory, topBSM.fr, is an unrelated MadGraph4-derived library of top-philic resonances (S0, O0, S1, O1, S2); it does not correspond to any model in this paper and is not the scored file. Residual (implementation-level, not model-level) risks for an agent reading only the paper: (a) it may drop O_uG because the paper says it 'contributes only at NLO'; (b) it may implement only the (1,3)/(3,1) u-t structures since the paper says it 'focuses' on them and calls the charm extension trivial; (c) it may apply the dim-4 counterterm shift of Eq. (12) (phi^dag phi - v^2/2) or implement only the tree-level tuh vertex of Eq. (8)/(11) instead of the full gauge-invariant operators; (d) yt normalisation conventions. None of these change field content or symmetry structure, so the paper is clearly single-model.
